section_summary: This section tracks Japanese naval movements in the western Pacific and Southeast Asia from May 1940 to March 1941. Much of the correspondence concerns the naval transport ASAKA’s passage through the Panama Canal, including security rules, Japanese objections, and its subsequent voyage to Europe. Reports also describe Japanese warships near Thailand, French Indochina, and the South China coast.

people.name: N. J. Wenermett
people.role: Press conference transcript signatory; name uncertain in OCR

people.name: Maxwell M. Hamilton
people.role: Chief, Division of Far Eastern Affairs

people.name: Southard
people.role: American diplomatic reporter at Hong Kong

people.name: Nakamura
people.role: Captain and senior aide to the Japanese Navy Minister

subfiles.title: Japanese Naval Force Proceeding to Palau
subfiles.about: Composition and planned movement of Japan’s Fourth Fleet toward Palau.
subfiles.summary: Lists ships, aircraft, and departure dates for a Japanese task force bound for Palau.

subfiles.title: Japanese Naval Forces Near Palau
subfiles.about: Navy authorities correct earlier reports about the size of Japanese forces near Palau.
subfiles.summary: Reports a small observation force near Palau and no alarming strategic significance.

subfiles.title: Reported Japanese Fleet Movements
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese fleet units near Yap, Saipan, and Palau and a southbound departure from Yokohama.
subfiles.summary: Relays British, Dutch, and local Japanese reports of fleet movements.

subfiles.title: Secretary’s Press Remarks on Fleet Movements
subfiles.about: Summarizes the Secretary’s answers about Japanese movements toward French Indochina and the U.S. fleet in Hawaiian waters.
subfiles.summary: Conveys the Secretary’s statement that he had no new official information.

subfiles.title: Press Conference Questions on Naval Movements
subfiles.about: Questions and answers concerning Japanese ships near French Indochina and the U.S. fleet at Hawaii.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary cites newspaper reports and says he has no new information about either fleet.

subfiles.title: Full Press Conference Transcript
subfiles.about: Transcript of questions on naval movements and other diplomatic matters.
subfiles.summary: Repeats the fleet questions and answers, then covers a Pan American conference, a political speech, France, and instructions to diplomats.

subfiles.title: Japanese Submarines Reported Bound for Hainan
subfiles.about: Intelligence reports fifteen Japanese submarines heading to Hainan to monitor U.S. naval activity.
subfiles.summary: Also reports a Japanese military headquarters on Hainan.

subfiles.title: Proposed Voyage of Naval Transport ASAKA
subfiles.about: Gives ASAKA’s planned route from Yokohama through the Panama Canal to Lisbon and back.
subfiles.summary: Requests notice to U.S. authorities of a voyage to repatriate citizens and exchange diplomatic personnel.

subfiles.title: ASAKA Notice to War Department Liaison
subfiles.about: Forwards the Japanese note concerning ASAKA’s proposed voyage.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the Japanese communication for War Department information.

subfiles.title: Request for War Department Courtesies
subfiles.about: Requests customary facilities for ASAKA if no objection is perceived.
subfiles.summary: Asks the War Department to extend usual courtesies.

subfiles.title: ASAKA Notice to Navy Department
subfiles.about: Forwards the Japanese note on ASAKA’s voyage.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the Japanese communication for Navy Department information.

subfiles.title: State Department Notice to Secretary of the Navy
subfiles.about: Reports ASAKA’s proposed Panama Canal passage and planned visit to Lisbon.
subfiles.summary: Sets out ASAKA’s itinerary and notes a request that War extend customary facilities.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of ASAKA Voyage Notice
subfiles.about: Acknowledges ASAKA’s proposed Canal transit and pending consultation with federal authorities.
subfiles.summary: Promises a further response after interested authorities reply.

subfiles.title: Reporting Large Japanese Vessels
subfiles.about: Points to instructions for reporting departures and arrivals of large Japanese vessels.
subfiles.summary: References a circular on reporting Japanese naval and merchant ships of at least 4,000 tons.

subfiles.title: Navy Response on ASAKA Transit
subfiles.about: States the Navy’s conditional lack of objection to ASAKA’s Canal transit.
subfiles.summary: Navy has no current objection if War Department security measures are followed.

subfiles.title: Draft Reply on Revised ASAKA Schedule
subfiles.about: Responds to ASAKA’s revised itinerary and consultations with federal authorities.
subfiles.summary: Notes the delayed voyage and reports no present objection, subject to conditions.

subfiles.title: Revised ASAKA Sailing Schedule
subfiles.about: Announces ASAKA’s delayed departure and revised Canal transit dates.
subfiles.summary: Departure moves to January 16, with transit toward Cristóbal around February 7.

subfiles.title: Armament and Status of ASAKA
subfiles.about: Describes ASAKA as a former liner now armed and flying a naval ensign.
subfiles.summary: Reports two probable six-inch guns and expected arrival at Panama about February 7.

subfiles.title: War Department Acknowledgment of ASAKA
subfiles.about: Acknowledges notice of ASAKA’s Canal visit.
subfiles.summary: Reports that the Panama Canal Department commander has been informed.

subfiles.title: ASAKA Radio Call Letters
subfiles.about: Supplies ASAKA’s radio call letters and signal code.
subfiles.summary: Identifies JMID and requests notification of the authorities concerned.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of ASAKA Radio Code
subfiles.about: Acknowledges ASAKA’s radio information.
subfiles.summary: Says copies were forwarded to federal authorities.

subfiles.title: ASAKA Radio Information to Navy
subfiles.about: Forwards the Japanese note giving ASAKA’s radio information.
subfiles.summary: Encloses ASAKA’s call letters and signal code.

subfiles.title: ASAKA Radio Information to War
subfiles.about: Forwards the Japanese note giving ASAKA’s radio information.
subfiles.summary: Encloses ASAKA’s call letters and signal code.

subfiles.title: Japanese Destroyer Near Bangkok
subfiles.about: Reports a Japanese destroyer near Bangkok.
subfiles.summary: Japanese officials cite communications with their legation and warships at Saigon.

subfiles.title: Japanese Objections to Armed Guards on ASAKA
subfiles.about: Japanese vice ministers contest armed guards during ASAKA’s Panama Canal passage.
subfiles.summary: Ohashi and Toyoda say notice of the security measure came too late to change ASAKA’s route and argue an armed guard would infringe warship privileges. They propose American naval officers aboard as guests. Grew reports his conversation and questions the claimed date on which Japan learned of the rule.

subfiles.title: Department’s Reply on Canal Security Rules
subfiles.about: Explains prior notice of armed guards and rejects a change to Panama Canal rules.
subfiles.summary: The Department says the Japanese naval attaché was warned on January 17 that armed guards would probably be required. It directs Grew to explain that the rules remain in force and have been applied to another foreign public vessel.

subfiles.title: Correction of Japanese Account of January Notice
subfiles.about: Disputes Japan’s assertion that State initially found no objection to ASAKA’s transit.
subfiles.summary: Staff confirm that State only said it was consulting federal authorities and had made no assurance of approval.

subfiles.title: Grew Reports Delivery of U.S. Position
subfiles.about: Reports informing Japan’s vice minister of the U.S. position on ASAKA.
subfiles.summary: Grew could not identify the other foreign vessel cited as precedent.

subfiles.title: Paraphrases of Grew’s ASAKA Telegram
subfiles.about: Restates Grew’s report of his exchange with Japan’s vice minister.
subfiles.summary: Records delivery of Washington’s position and the unanswered question about another foreign vessel.

subfiles.title: Japanese Proposal for Liaison Officer Aboard ASAKA
subfiles.about: Proposes a U.S. liaison officer and pistol-carrying attendants aboard ASAKA.
subfiles.summary: Suggests keeping the U.S. party on the upper deck with cooperation from Japan’s naval attaché.

subfiles.title: Conversation with Japanese Chargé on ASAKA Security
subfiles.about: Records Morishima’s proposed alternative to an armed guard on ASAKA.
subfiles.summary: Morishima proposes a U.S. officer and pistol-carrying attendants aboard during transit. Hamilton recommends that Japanese military and naval attachés discuss practical arrangements directly with their U.S. counterparts.

subfiles.title: Japanese Thanks for ASAKA Reception
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese appreciation for ASAKA’s reception at the Canal.
subfiles.summary: Japanese officials say ASAKA passed through without incident and received a warm welcome.

subfiles.title: Cruiser Movement at Saigon
subfiles.about: Reports ABUKUMA’s departure following another Japanese cruiser’s arrival.
subfiles.summary: ABUKUMA left Saigon after NAGARA arrived.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Saigon Cruiser Report
subfiles.about: Restates the report of Japanese cruiser movements at Saigon.
subfiles.summary: Notes ABUKUMA’s departure and asks for repetition of an earlier missing telegram.

subfiles.title: Australian Report on Japanese Fleet in Gulf of Siam
subfiles.about: Relays Australian concern about Japanese naval units and possible bases in Southeast Asia.
subfiles.summary: Latham reports Japanese units near the Gulf of Siam and Saigon, with rumors of demands for bases at Cam Ranh and Songkhla. He considers occupation a threat to Singapore and proposes seeking an explanation from Japan.

subfiles.title: Hornbeck’s Reply to Australian Legation
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the Australian naval intelligence report.
subfiles.summary: Thanks Watt and sends good wishes to the hospitalized Australian Minister.

subfiles.title: Instruction to Report Japanese Naval Movements
subfiles.about: Requests prompt reporting of Japanese naval vessels and troop movements.
subfiles.summary: Instructs the consul to use discreetly obtainable information.

subfiles.title: Hong Kong Reporting Difficulties
subfiles.about: Explains limits on verification of Japanese movement reports.
subfiles.summary: Southard requests an additional officer and code clerk to investigate plausible rumors.

subfiles.title: Japanese Ships and Troops at Daya Bay
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese carriers, cruisers, transports, and troop activity in Daya Bay.
subfiles.summary: Several vessels are reported at the bay, some later sailing south. Japanese troops appear focused on loading captured trade goods, while guerrillas remain active and Huizhou has apparently not been occupied.

subfiles.title: Japanese Destroyer Visits to Pak Nam
subfiles.about: Reports Thai permission for three Japanese destroyers to obtain supplies near Bangkok.
subfiles.summary: The ships form part of a larger fleet described officially as patrolling under the Saigon truce.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Pak Nam Destroyer Report
subfiles.about: Restates the report of Japanese destroyers visiting Pak Nam.
subfiles.summary: Cites replenishment and truce patrol duties.

subfiles.title: Japanese Fleet in Gulf of Siam
subfiles.about: Reports a nineteen-ship Japanese fleet near Thai territorial waters.
subfiles.summary: Places the fleet near Sattahip and Ko Sichang and links Bangkok-area destroyers to it.

subfiles.title: Daya Bay Situation, Corrected Copy
subfiles.about: Updates reports on Japanese forces and shipping at Daya Bay.
subfiles.summary: Southard reports limited fighting, some reinforcements, and possibly 10,000 Japanese troops. Captured commodities continue to be loaded aboard ships, while distant observations have prompted unconfirmed rumors of base construction.

subfiles.title: Daya Bay Situation, Earlier Copy
subfiles.about: Earlier copy of the Daya Bay situation report.
subfiles.summary: Repeats reports of reinforcements, captured cargo loading, and uncertain base construction.

subfiles.title: Japanese Naval Vessel Movements Reference
subfiles.about: Points to another telegram reporting Japanese naval vessel movements.
subfiles.summary: Cross-references a Saigon report by Flood.

subfiles.title: Southbound Japanese Transports
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese transports departing southward in early February.
subfiles.summary: An ordinarily trustworthy source says thirty-seven transports left Japan February 1–15.

subfiles.title: ASAKA’s Possible Return via Suez
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese inquiry about returning ASAKA through the Suez Canal.
subfiles.summary: Captain Nakamura asked the British naval attaché whether ASAKA might use Suez and refuel at Colombo to avoid another Panama Canal dispute. The attaché doubted Britain would allow passage and discussed worsening Anglo-Japanese relations.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Suez Inquiry
subfiles.about: Restates Nakamura’s inquiry about ASAKA’s return through Suez.
subfiles.summary: Records British doubts about allowing the ship through the canal.

subfiles.title: Grew Despatch on ASAKA Canal Passage
subfiles.about: Transmits records of conversations and an oral statement concerning ASAKA.
subfiles.summary: Encloses accounts of Grew’s February 1 and 3 meetings with Japanese vice ministers and the U.S. statement on Canal security.

subfiles.title: Conversation with Ohashi and Toyoda
subfiles.about: Records Japanese objections to armed guards aboard ASAKA.
subfiles.summary: Ohashi and Toyoda recount their understanding of U.S. notices, say guards would violate warship privileges, and propose American naval officers aboard as guests. Grew agrees to relay their views while observing that an executive rule would presumably apply to all foreign warships.

subfiles.title: Conversation with Ohashi on U.S. Reply
subfiles.about: Records Grew’s delivery of the U.S. response on ASAKA.
subfiles.summary: Ohashi asks the nationality of a vessel previously subject to the rule; Grew cannot say.

subfiles.title: Oral Statement on ASAKA Security Rules
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew for the U.S. Government
subfiles.to: Japanese Vice Minister for Foreign Affairs
subfiles.about: States that Panama Canal armed-guard rules remain in force.
subfiles.summary: Recounts January notice to Japan’s naval attaché and says another foreign public vessel accepted the rules.

subfiles.title: File Note on ASAKA Arrival in Lisbon
subfiles.about: Summarizes Lisbon’s despatch on the Japanese officers carried by ASAKA.
subfiles.summary: Notes 111 officers headed toward Berlin, some through Italy.

subfiles.title: Japanese Navy Transport ASAKA at Lisbon
subfiles.about: Reports ASAKA’s arrival at Lisbon and the movements of its Japanese officer passengers.
subfiles.summary: ASAKA arrived February 20 with 111 Japanese army and navy officers, including three rear admirals. They planned to reach Berlin by routes through France and Italy, observe Axis military facilities, and in some cases train on German aircraft. ASAKA left after three days.

subfiles.title: Japanese Naval Mission in Rome
subfiles.about: Reports part of the Japanese naval mission in Rome.
subfiles.summary: Identifies Admiral Abe as leader of the Rome group.

subfiles.title: Telephone Conversation on ASAKA Passage
subfiles.about: Records a telephone reply to Morishima about ASAKA’s Canal passage.
subfiles.summary: Directs Japan’s naval attaché to contact Navy for an explanation of the security rules.

subfiles.title: ASAKA Cargo Inquiry
subfiles.about: Answers an inquiry about whether ASAKA carried cargo.
subfiles.summary: Canal Zone authorities report that ASAKA carried no cargo.

subfiles.title: Fifteenth Naval District Report on ASAKA
subfiles.about: Provides information on ASAKA’s personnel and voyage.
subfiles.summary: OCR is badly damaged; the memorandum appears to identify officers aboard ASAKA bound for Lisbon.

subfiles.title: Japanese Warship Change at Saigon
subfiles.about: Reports replacement of a Japanese cruiser by a destroyer at Saigon.
subfiles.summary: The destroyer ISOKAZE replaced the cruiser, apparently ABUKUMA, on March 14.

subfiles.title: Navy Relay of Saigon Warship Report
subfiles.about: Relays Saigon’s report of the Japanese warship change.
subfiles.summary: Confidential teletype repeats that ISOKAZE replaced a cruiser on March 14.
